description.narrative: ESDP III is proposed as the third program in the sequence of education sector development programs. It will build upon and extend the achievements of ESDP I and ESDP II. A key lesson learned from these programs is that rapid expansion of the education system needs to be matched equally with quality improvement. While EEQP addresses this through secondary teacher and curriculum development, there are substantial unmet needs at the lower secondary level, in particular.

description.narrative: Increased lower secondary enrollment

LS Net Enrollment Rate is increased by 5% (7% girls). (Baseline SY2010/11: 35% (37.2% girls) Progress/Status: LS Net Enrollment Rate has been increased from 41.9% (F. 46.4%) for SY2015/16 to 44.0% (F.48.9%) which is by 9% (11.7% girls).

Lower Secondary Gross Enrollment Rate is increased by 5% (7% girls). (Baseline SY2010/11: 58.5% (57.8% girls) Progress/Status: The lower secondary gross enrolment has been increased from 53.3% (F. 55.3%) in school year 2014/15 to 53.8% (F. 56.7%) in school year 2015/16, to 55.3% (F. 59.6%) in school year 2016/17, and to 56.8% (F. 61.0%) in school year 2017/18. Despite GER for girl is higher (60.0%) compared to the baseline (57.8%), overall GER remains lower than the baseline in school year 2010/11 at 58.5%.
Nevertheless, GER in school year 2017/18 is higher than the government's revised education sector's target which is 54.6% (F. 57.5%) Data Source: Provincial EMIS
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: At least 100 Technical Group Leaders or Senior Teacher in math trained (25% female). Core competency of 80% trained Technical Group Leaders (TDL) or Senior Teachers in mathematics trained (25% female). Progress/Status: 153 (24 female, 16% ) mathematics (TGLs or senior teachers) from 151 schools were trained in mathematics techniques. 100% of female TGLs or senior teachers were trained. Data Source: Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: At least 100 schools implement employability skills program, with 50% female participation. Progress/Status: Approximately 133 schools from 14 provinces are implementing employability skills programs. Data Source: Survey School Reports or progress report Actual value:

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: At least 400 lower secondary science teachers trained (25% female). Progress/Status: 592 (210 females or 35.5%) science teachers trained, from 151 schools. Data Source: Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: At least 90% of lower secondary math and science teachers (25% female) trained to implement student-centered / inquiry-based teaching techniques. Progress/Status: All mathematics and science teachers in 151 schools from 14 provinces received training in implementing student centered and inquiry-based teaching techniques.
592 (210 female, 35.4%) teachers were science trained, and 153 (24 female, 16%) mathematics teachers were trained. A total of 745 (234 female, 31.4%) lower secondary math and science teachers were trained (2017 & 2018). Data Source: Pre- and Post-Training Assessment or progress report Actual value:

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: At least 80% of lower secondary School Directors/Deputy Directors (100% of current female School Directors/Deputy Directors) implement School Improvement Plans (inclusive of gender equity dimensions) and manage school operating budgets by 2014. Progress/Status: Completed.
At least 80% of lower secondary school directors'/deputy directors' (100% of current female school directors'/deputy directors) implemented school improvement plans (inclusive of gender equity dimensions) and manage school operating budget. Data Source: Post-workshop evaluation or progress report Actual value:

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Findings from 8 action research studies, inclusive of gender and equity dimensions presented to ESWG and disseminated throughout MoEYS Progress/Status: Completed.
An impact study and an action research (each has 4 research topics) were completed. Data Source: Pilot Evaluation and ESWG minutes Actual value:

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Project in target provinces, by 2017 At least 200 lower secondary school directors/deputy directors trained (100% of current female school directors/deputy directors) Progress/Status: Completed.
The School Director Professional Development (SDPD) materials, approved in July 2017 and uploaded on the web http://esdp3sdpd.weebly.com for school management and teachers access, were used for school management trainings. In total, 300 (7% female or 100% of available female school management) LSS directors and deputy directors, including additional 100 LSS directors under the project's extension period were trained. Data Source: Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: School Support Committees of at least 60% of lower secondary schools are involved in monitoring the use of school budget. Progress/Status: Completed.
The guidelines and training materials for secondary school support committee (SSC), approved in August 2017, were distributed to 250 LSSs, including additional 50 schools under the project's extended period. Approximately, 64 target schools established SSCs (more than 79% female member). Data Source: Post-workshop evaluation or progress report Actual value:

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: Project in target provinces, by 2017: at least 80% (60% female) students identified as at-risk of school dropout transition to next grade (baseline to be determined). Progress/Status: On average approximately 10% of the total student population are identified as ‘at risk' in the target schools. Of these approximately 50% are promoted following additional tuition and support. AR girls are less likely to be promoted than AR boys (45.5% of AR girls were promoted). Data Source: School Reports and data to be collected Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Number of female teachers staffed in lower secondary schools increased by 10%. (SY2010/11 Baseline: 38.6%) Progress/Status: Number of female teacher staff in lower secondary schools in 2016/17 increased by 6.7% or 13,026 female teachers (43% of lower secondary teachers are female) Data Source: MoEYS EMIS and Project Report Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Number of students aged 12-14 enrolled in lower secondary school increased by 10%, including 10% female students. (SY2010/11 Baseline: 507,207 (297,648 females) Progress/Status: Partially achieved. Number of students aged 12-14 enrolled in lower secondary schools increased by 6.5% (F. 7.3%). Total Students 12-14 enrolled in lower secondary schools in 2017/2018: 469,310 [254, 210 females].
The actual 2010/2011 baseline = 440,660 (236,750 females 53.7%). Data Source: MoEYS-EMIS Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Project in target provinces, by 2017, at least 44 new lower secondary schools constructed Progress/Status: Achieved. All of the revised target 44 new LSSs constructed and received establishment packages for immediate start-up. Data Source: Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: At least 544 new lower secondary classrooms constructed Progress/Status: Achieved. All the revised target 544 new LSS classrooms constructed. Data Source: Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Transition rate from Grade 6 to Grade 7 is increased by 10% (10% female students). (SY2010/11 Baseline: 80.2% total / 81.3% female) Progress/Status: Transition rate from grade 6 to grade 7 is increased by 8.5 from baseline (transition rate 2017/18 is 88.5% ) and increased by 8.7% from baseline for female student). Data Source: MoEYS EMIS Actual value:

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Daily student attendance in lower secondary school improves for both males and females. Progress/Status: The results of the survey with target schools shows an increase in absences of 2.1%, from 4.9% in 2017 to 7% in 2018. Data Source: Project Report base on assessment Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Prakas for establishment packages issued by 2013. Progress/Status: Achieved. Prakas 2195 Establishment Packages endorsed on August 6, 2014 and Implementation plan signed 11 September 2014. Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Expanded access to lower secondary education Indicator: Quality control guidelines for new school building construction, inclusive of gender sensitive sanitation facilities issued by 2012. Progress/Status: Achieved. Completed quality control guidelines published in 2012/13 Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: Guidelines for basic education progression program issued by 2013. Progress/Status: Achieved. • Guidelines for basic education progression program Prakas 218, DoF issued in December 2013 • Guideline on use of SIG for school progression issued December 13, 2013. • ESP 2014-2018 endorsed on March 07, 2014 by Minister of Education Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improved quality of lower secondary education Indicator: Prakas for adapting sex-disaggregated Grade 9 Gross Completion Rate at provincial level as Core Breakthrough Indicator issued by 2013. Progress/Status: Achieved. 53% of provinces have achieved completion rate > 40% in 2014/15 Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Action plan developed for school performance monitoring system, with indicators reporting on gender specific issues, by 2014. Progress/Status: Completed. Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Guidelines issued for establishing school support committees, with 40% female representation, by 2014. Progress/Status: Completed. Data Source: Provincial Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Prakas issued to adopt new School Operating Budget funding mechanism, inclusive of School Improvement Grants by 2014. Progress/Status: Completed. Data Source: MoEYS Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y

Output: Improved sub-sector management Indicator: Primary and lower secondary schools within pilot basic education School Clusters implement student progression plan, with an emphasis on ensuring progression of female students through Grades 1-9. Progress/Status: Completed.
The guidelines for strengthening the secondary education school cluster, approved in May 2017, were distributed to the 250 target LSSs. The guidelines provide a platform for schools to strengthen the school management/leadership and performance and knowledge of subject teachers across clusters of schools. In total, 300 (54% female) school directors and deputy directors from 150 LSSs were trained on the approved guidelines and techniques of leading ESC. Approximately, 49 target schools established ESCs. Data Source: Pre- and Post-Training Evaluation or progress report Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y
